32 The diagram shows a circuit with a light-dependent resistor (LDR).
10 k
6.0 k
A
12 V
30 k
The ammeter reads zero current.
What is the resistance of the LDR?
A
6.0 k
B
18 k
C
26 k
D
30 k

hints: Notice the ammeter joins the middle of the left $10\text{ k}\Omega$ - $30\text{ k}\Omega$ branch and the middle of the right $6.0\text{ k}\Omega$ - LDR branch, and it reads zero.
Zero current means no potential difference across the ammeter, so the two potential dividers must give the same voltage at the two middle points.
Set the left voltage ratio equal to the right voltage ratio using $10\text{ k}\Omega$, $30\text{ k}\Omega$, $6.0\text{ k}\Omega$ and the LDR resistance, then solve for the LDR.
walkthrough: Identify the bridge: left arm is $10\text{ k}\Omega$ over $30\text{ k}\Omega$, right arm is $6.0\text{ k}\Omega$ over $R_{LDR}$, both across the same $12\text{ V}$ supply.
Use the zero-current condition: no current in the middle wire means the left middle point and right middle point are at the same potential.
For the same potential, the resistance ratios must match: $R_{top,left}/R_{bottom,left} = R_{top,right}/R_{bottom,right}$.
Substitute values with units: $10\text{ k}\Omega / 30\text{ k}\Omega = 6.0\text{ k}\Omega / R_{LDR}$.

A.explanation: Confuses the top resistors only. $6.0\text{ k}\Omega$ would balance $10\text{ k}\Omega$ against $10\text{ k}\Omega$, not against $30\text{ k}\Omega$.

B.explanation: Balanced bridge gives $10/30 = 6.0/R$, so $R = 18\text{ k}\Omega$ and both middle points are at the same potential.

C.explanation: Adds $20\text{ k}\Omega$ difference incorrectly. Resistance ratios must be equal, not resistances added or subtracted.

D.explanation: Assumes the LDR must equal the opposite $30\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor, ignoring the $10\text{ k}\Omega$ to $6.0\text{ k}\Omega$ ratio on the top arms.
